questions: Should the model be trained on the entire dataset (X, y) before returning, or only trained on the last fold's training data from cross-validation?
Is the cross-validation score computed using the default scoring metric of RandomForestRegressor (R^2) or some other metric?
Should the random_seed parameter control both the data generation (numpy) and the model's random_state, or only one of them?
If cv is not an integer, should it be interpreted as a number of folds or as a custom cross-validation splitter object?
Should the function return the mean cross-validation score as a Python float or a numpy float?
Is the target noise independent per sample (as in reference) or could it be a single noise value added to all samples?
Should the model's n_estimators be set exactly to the provided parameter, or is there a default if not provided?
If random_seed is None, should the numpy random seed be set to None (leaving global state unchanged) or omitted?
